main_text.l: Isaac, & posteris suis tradidit. Gen. 25. v. 2. c. 26. v. 25. c.
28. v. 1. 2. 3. 4. Jacob quoque habuit scholam suam priuatam:
48. & 49. Post Jacobum scholae priuatae, siue domesticae
institutiones, in Aegypto perdurarunt usque ad mortem
Josephi. Gen. 50. v. 23. Post Josephum vero, cum populus
Israëliticus mirum in modum augeretur, ita ut domesti-
ca institutio sufficere non posset, quaelibet tribus procul
dubio habuit scholas suas, non sublatis tamen domesticis
scholis. Porrò postquam populus ex Aegypto in desertum fuit e-
ductus, Moses & Aharon fuerunt primi doctores scholae
publicae & universalis. Deut. 4. verf. 14. c. 5.
v. 1. 7: Confer Exod. 20. & seqq. Interim tamen scholae priuatae domesti-
cae non fuerunt sublatae, sed confirmatae. Deut. 6. v. 6. c. 4.
v. 10. c. 11. v. 19. Exod. 12. v. 24. & seqq. Schola Mosis & A-
haronis peperit scholas Leuitarum, quae fuerunt ordinariae,
& duratunt usque ad excidium Hierosolymitanum per
Titum. Act. 13. v. 14. & seqq. Deut. 17. v. 8. c. 18. v. 7. 1. Chron.
13. 14. 15. 17. Praeter has Leuitarum scholas ordinarias
fuerunt etiam scholae extraordinariae prophetarum, ut constat
mus nunc scholas N. T. ubi praeter scholas Judaeorum, &
nominatim Pharisaeorum Matth. 22. v. 15. 16. Johan. 3. v.
10: primo occurrit schola Johannis Baptistae Matth. 11. verf. 2.
Joh. 1. v. 28. deinde schola Christi Johan. 18. v. 19. 20. deni-
que scholae apostolorum Act. 13. 15. 20. 2. Tim. 2. & 3.
IV. Modus utendi his exemplaribus conti-
netur sequentibus regulis. 1. Patresfamilias & ma-
gistratus Christiani debent in hoc incumbere, ut insti-
tuant & foveant scholas: exemplo patriarcharum, Mosis,
Samuelis, Davidis, & Salomonis. Gen. 18. v. 19. Deut. 4. v. 14.
29. v. 25. & seqq. 2. Scholae aliae sint priuatae & domesticae,
aliae publicae. Illae his subserviant, hae illas confirment:

page.notes: Line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 stand in the left margin. They are line counters, not text, so I left them out. The running head and the catchword are read from the scan. "Isaac" starts with a consonant I, but I kept it as printed rather than changing it to "Jsaac". The "IV." opening is set italic and indented, so I treated it as a paragraph opener, not a heading. Verse numbers such as "verf." and "c." are copied as printed.
